clues.title: Plate: orange dot on the left
text: Andorran licence plates have an **orange dot** on the left side and can be regularly found throughout the country.
NOTE: Within Europe, this plate is unique to Andorra.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: European plate with an orange dot on its left side. No other European country uses it, so it gives the country away.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 3 with medium-short antenna
text: Andorra **only has Generation 2 and Generation 3** coverage. In all Generation 3 coverage, a medium-short antenna is visible on the Google car.
Generation 3 is by far the most common. Almost all of Generation 2 is overwritten and is mostly confined to a couple of smaller off-roads.

images.caption: Google car antennas: Gen 2 (rare, left) and Gen 3 (right); circle zooms in on the antenna

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Only Gen 2 and Gen 3 exist. Gen 3 shows a medium-short antenna on the car and is by far the most common. Gen 2 is rare, mostly small side roads.

clues.title: Coverage: autumn colours everywhere
text: All the Generation 3 coverage was taken in October, meaning that many deciduous trees have **autumn colours**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: All Gen 3 coverage was taken in October, so many leafy trees are orange and yellow.

clues.title: Houses: stone buildings
text: Andorra has a lot of these **stone** buildings. They can be seen almost everywhere in the country.
NOTE: These buildings can also be found close to Andorra, in the French and Spanish Pyrenees.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Stone buildings are everywhere. The same style appears in the French and Spanish Pyrenees, so it narrows things down but is not conclusive.

clues.title: Pole: wooden snow poles, mixed colours
text: Andorran snow poles are made out of **wood** and can have a variety** **of** colours** on them.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Snow poles are made of wood and can be painted in many different colours.

clues.title: Language: Catalan, with i instead of y
text: **Catalan** is the main language in Andorra. It is a Romance language that is closely related to Spanish and French.

If you are unfamiliar with Romance languages, it can be hard to distinguish between Catalan and Spanish. If you see **i** instead of **y** (“and” in English), it is Catalan. In addition, more Catalan words end with consonants.
NOTE: The Catalan language is also used in eastern Spain: in Catalonia, the Valencian community and the Balearic islands.

images.caption: Sample of Catalan text, with i used where Spanish has y

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Catalan looks like Spanish, but it writes i where Spanish writes y ("and") and has more words ending in consonants. Also used in eastern Spain.

clues.title: Language: carrer means street
text: The Catalan word for street is **“carrer”**.

images.caption: Street sign reading CARRER DE LA BORDA; carrer means street in Catalan

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The Catalan word for street is carrer. Seeing it on a sign points to Catalan-speaking areas.

clues.title: Sign: km markers with CG and CS numbers
text: These kilometre markers with** CG and CS **road numbers are found in Andorra.
NOTE: Similar kilometre marker designs can be found in Spain.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Kilometre markers show road numbers starting with CG or CS. Spain has similar marker designs, so check other clues too.

clues.title: Guardrail: yellow reflectors
text: Andorra uses **yellow** reflectors on its guardrails.
NOTE: Within Europe, yellow reflectors are only found in Andorra, Spain and Belgium. For a good overview of European guardrails, see [this infographic](/images/andorra/europeguardrail.png).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Guardrails have yellow reflectors. In Europe only this country, Spain and Belgium use yellow, so it narrows things down.

clues.title: Bollard: orange reflector
text: The Andorran bollard has an **orange** reflector and can be occasionally found on the main highways.
NOTE: This bollard can also be found in **Spain**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Bollard with an orange reflector, seen now and then on the main highways. Spain uses the same one.

clues.title: Road works: yellow and turquoise cones
text: **Yellow** and **turquoise-green** traffic cones are used in the whole country.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Traffic cones in yellow and turquoise-green are used across the whole country.

clues.title: Sign: pedestrian sign with 8 stripes
text: Pedestrian signs** **have **8 stripes**.
NOTE: Spain is the only other European country that has pedestrian signs with 8 stripes.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The pedestrian crossing sign has 8 stripes on the crosswalk. Spain is the only other European country with 8.

clues.title: Google car: many Gen 2 snow trekkers
text: Andorra has a lot of Generation 2 **snow trekkers**, especially on ski resorts.
NOTE: Other countries have snow trekkers as well, but Andorra has the highest amount for its size.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Lots of older Gen 2 coverage taken on foot or by snow vehicle, especially at ski resorts. More than any other country for its size.

clues.title: Landscape: capital in a high mountain valley
text: **Andorra la Vella** is a capital city surrounded by high mountains, making it recognisable.
NOTE: It is the highest European capital with an altitude of 1023 metres.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The capital is a city surrounded by tall mountains. At 1023 m it is the highest capital in Europe.

clues.title: Landmark: Caldea tower and sky wheel
text: In the capital Andorra la Vella you can often see the **Caldea tower** and the **sky wheel**.

images.caption: Caldea glass tower and a tall sky wheel behind it

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the capital you often see the tall Caldea spa tower and a sky wheel (Ferris wheel).

clues.title: Town: ski town with shops, no trees
text: **Pas de la Casa**, a touristy city in eastern Andorra, can be easily recognized by the plethora of shops and hotels. As it is located at an altitude of 2080 metres, there are no trees visible on the mountains surrounding it.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the east, a touristy town packed with shops and hotels. At 2080 m, the surrounding mountains have no trees.
